cards.front: Recall a key point about Forces and Stresses on Materials
cards.back: Tension: pulling force that stretches - ropes, cables, bridge wires. Compression: pushing force that squashes - columns, arches, foam packaging.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Forces and Stresses on Materials
cards.back: Bending: combines tension (outer surface stretches) and compression (inner surface squashes) - I-beams concentrate material at flanges where forces are greatest.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Forces and Stresses on Materials
cards.back: Shear: forces in opposite directions parallel to a surface - scissors, bolted joints. Torsion: twisting force - drive shafts, screwdrivers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Forces and Stresses on Materials
cards.back: Stress = Force / Area (N/m2). Strain = Change in length / Original length. Young's Modulus = Stress / Strain (measures stiffness).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Forces and Stresses on Materials
cards.back: Factor of Safety (FoS) = Ultimate strength / Working stress. Typical: 2-4 non-critical, 5-10 safety-critical. Higher FoS = safer but heavier and more expensive.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For forces/stress questions: 1) Identify force type, 2) Explain where it occurs, 3) State relevant formula, 4) Calculate if required, 5) Relate to design decisions.
Tension + compression (e.g. Failure on tension face)
Sliding in parallel planes (e.g. Clean angled break)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: If a material is strong, it will not break under any type of force. Correct: 'Strong' depends on force type. Concrete has excellent compressive strength (20-40 MPa) but very poor tensile strength (2-5 MPa). That is why reinforced concrete adds steel rebar in the tension zone. Always specify: strong in WHAT? Tension? Compression? Shear?
A designer is creating a lightweight folding chair. Explain how tension, compression and bending act on the chair, and justify the material choices for the frame and seat.

AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). For grade 9, demonstrate precise understanding of force types and perceptive analysis of force distribution.

cards.front: Types of Forces and Their Effects
cards.back: Five primary types of force act on materials in products: tension (pulling, stretching), compression (pushing, squashing), bending (combination of tension and compression across a cross-section), shear (sliding forces acting in parallel planes), and torsion (twisting).
